native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (jailed 1985-1994) had significantly lower wealth than those without a record in all three years — 1985, 1990, and 1996 (all unadjusted and adjusted p<0.05). The gap widened over time (mean difference ~-$17k in 1985, ~-$58k in 1990, ~-$85k in 1996; jailed-group medians $720/$0/$0 vs $3,600/$10,500/$8,500). Because ever_jailed covers only 1985-1994, the significant 1985 gap reflects pre-existing (pre-incarceration) differences, while 1990 and 1996 — especially the larger 1996 gap — are consistent with wealth divergence during and after incarceration. This is an association, not a causal claim.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data (12,013 rows, zero missing); verified negatives in all wealth years (net worth interpretation). Per-year two-group comparisons (ever_jailed 1 vs 0, n=289 vs 11,724): Welch t-tests, one/two-sided Mann-Whitney U, winsorized (1%/99%) t-test sensitivity; adjusted HC3-robust OLS and median (quantile) regression with race and sex covariates ('hipanic' mapped for modeling only, original values untouched); stratified race×sex descriptives with underpowered-cell flags. Verdict at alpha=0.05: all three years significant on every test; timing interpretation: 1985 pre-incarceration selection, 1990 during-window, 1996 post-incarceration.

sub_hypo.text: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, with wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 (ever_jailed = 1) have significantly lower composite wealth in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996 than individuals not jailed during that period (ever_jailed = 0).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 had significantly lower wealth in 1985, 1990, and 1996 than individuals not jailed in that period, both before and after adjustment for race and sex.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort; 12,013 respondents, including 289 jailed between 1985 and 1994 and 11,724 not jailed during that period.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed status was associated with lower wealth in each year, with all unadjusted and adjusted tests significant at p<0.05. Comparisons included Welch t-tests, one- and two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests, 1%/99% winsorized t-tests, and HC3-robust OLS and median regression adjusted for race and sex. Wealth includes negative values and is interpreted as net worth.

sub_hypo.text: The wealth gap between individuals jailed in 1985–1994 and those not jailed during that period widened across 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort; wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996, with jailed status defined over 1985–1994.
sub_hypo.relations: Mean wealth differences, jailed minus not jailed, were approximately −$17,000 in 1985, −$58,000 in 1990, and −$85,000 in 1996. Jailed-group medians were $720, $0, and $0, versus $3,600, $10,500, and $8,500 for the non-jailed group, respectively.

sub_hypo.text: The significant 1985 wealth gap reflects pre-existing, pre-incarceration differences, while the 1990 and 1996 gaps, especially the larger 1996 gap, are consistent with wealth divergence during and after incarceration rather than establishing a causal effect.
sub_hypo.context: National Longitudinal Study of Youth 1979 cohort; ever_jailed covers only 1985–1994. The workflow interprets 1985 as pre-incarceration selection, 1990 as during-window, and 1996 as post-incarceration.
sub_hypo.relations: The timing of the wealth differences is interpreted as pre-existing selection in 1985 and divergence during and after the incarceration window in 1990 and 1996. These relationships are associations, not causal claims.
